Robin Bhowmik, CEO of Adani Group’s Skills and Education wing, participates in a conference on Viksit Bharat in Vijayawada on Thursday. | Photo Credit: G.N. RAO
India’s journey towards becoming a developed nation depends on skill development, technological advancement and strengthening domestic production, Adani Group CEO (Skills and Education) Robin Bhowmick has said.
Addressing the inaugural session of the 7th International Conference on Viksit Bharat, jointly organised by P.B. Siddhartha College of Arts and Science and the Indian Economics and Allied Sciences Association at P.V.P. Siddhartha Engineering College, here, on Thursday, Mr. Bhowmick emphasised the need for self-reliance and self-sufficiency.
He urged the youth to develop technical skills, adapt to automation and make productive use of their time to contribute to the nation’s progress.
The progress of the country, he said, cannot be measured by the yardstick of technology imported from China.
“In this age of automation, we must rise technologically. The mindset of the youth must undergo transformation,” he said and advised young people to nurture a scientific temperament and become the architects of a truly developed India.
Siddhartha Academy president Malineni Rajaiah expressed confidence that Amaravati would emerge as a major national hub within a decade.
Academy joint secretary Nimmagadda Lalitha Prasad called for a debate on population growth and raised concerns over the GST system’s impact on the middle class.
The session was attended by several academicians and dignitaries, including P.V.P. Siddhartha Engineering College Principal K. Sivaji Babu and academic advisor L.K. Mohan Rao, who proposed establishing an Adani Group Skill Centre at Siddhartha.
Research awards were presented to R.K. Mishra and A.A. Sheikh, while the Academic Excellence Award was conferred on L.K. Mohan Rao. Mr. Bhowmick unveiled a souvenir featuring 106 research papers and several books.
The event also featured research paper presentations chaired by former Vice-Chancellor of Kuvempu University B.P. Veerabhadrappa. Stellenbosch University Professor R.K. Mishra delivered the memorial lecture in honour of late Dr. I.G. Patel.
